title: Queue watermarking and causal-correlation ordered delivery for structured log aggregation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Structured log ingestion for high-throughput tenants occasionally delivers events out of causal order when front-end multiplexers and asynchronous buffering are used. This causes traces and dashboards (latency percentiles and error counts) to show inconsistent timelines for correlated spans and log lines, which impacts incident debugging and SLO correctness. Existing solutions (strict per-tenant single-writer shards) are expensive and fragile under bursty loads.

Goal: Implement a lightweight queue watermarking layer and causal-correlation delivery guarantees for the ingestion pipeline that preserves causal ordering for correlated events (per-request correlation-id or trace-id semantics) while tolerating out-of-order arrival across independent requests. The feature should work with our Loki-compatible ingestion path and integrate with existing prefix/KV cache and tenant fanout. It must provide a bounded buffering window, backpressure hints to upstream proxies, and an operational dashboard to surface stalled watermarks and ordering replays.
technical_design:
High-level approach:

1) Watermark tokens: Every incoming structured event gets assigned a logical ingest sequence combined with an estimated event timestamp; for events that include correlation keys (trace_id, corr_id, request_id) we attach a lightweight correlation vector derived from the trace span hierarchy (vector-clock-like nonce built from span parent pointers limited to 2 hops). These are encoded in the ingest envelope metadata (header fields) and are serialized as compact base64 to avoid payload bloat.

2) Per-tenant causal buffers: For each tenant shard we maintain small, bounded per-correlation buffer keyed by correlation id (hot paths) and a general out-of-order buffer for non-correlated events. Each per-correlation buffer uses the watermark to release events once monotonicity is safe (either seeing a later watermark or receiving an explicit end-of-request marker). Buffers are capped (configurable default 64 events or 2MB) with overflow policies: emit best-effort (with out-of-order flag) or force backpressure when policy=strict.

3) Watermark advancement: Watermarks advance based on a hybrid approach: (a) observed event timestamps from upstream, (b) sequence gaps (if sequence numbers supplied), and (c) periodic heartbeat markers from frontends/proxies. Watermarks are propagated down to the storage writers so Loki/ES writers can preserve ordering tags and enable compaction optimizations.

4) Backpressure and hinting: When a tenant's buffers approach capacity we emit explicit backpressure hints via the existing ingress protocol (HTTP 429 with Retry-After and X-Log-Watermark header). Dedicated capacity customers can opt into cooperative throttling where we coordinate with autoscaling to allocate burst capacity before shedding events.

5) Operational surfaces: Add metrics for watermark lag (ms), per-correlation buffer sizes, number of forced-ordered-emits, and percentage of events delivered with 'ordering_suspect' flag. Add dashboard panels to Console for per-tenant watermark heatmaps, top offending correlation ids, and trend lines for out-of-order deliveries.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We avoid full vector clocks to minimize metadata; correlation vector is intentionally limited depth to handle typical web request trees.
- Strict guarantees are per-correlation id only; cross-correlation causal chains (e.g., async fan-out across services with new correlation ids) are out of scope for this ticket.
- Default policy will be 'best-effort with hinting' to minimize customer-visible latency regressions; strict ordering mode is opt-in and billed.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented ingestion path emits watermark and correlation metadata headers for >95% of structured log flows in staging
Per-tenant dashboard shows watermark lag and buffer occupancy; panels added to Console ingest observability section
Controlled experiment: for a synthetic workload with injected causal ordering, we achieve >99.9% in-order delivery for correlated events under normal load and >=95% during 2x bursts (strict mode off)
Backpressure path exercised end-to-end: upstream proxy honors X-Log-Watermark and 429 hints in integration test
No more than 2% P50 latency regression on critical 95th-percentile path for hosted customers when feature enabled (measured in runtime-1.20 canary)
Feature toggle implemented; migration plan documented and rollout can be selectively enabled per-tenant
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Implement feature flag gated on tenant attribute; deploy to canary cluster with internal tenants only. Monitor watermark lag and ordering_suspect metrics for 72 hours.

Phase 2 (staged): Enable default best-effort mode for 10% production tenants. Collect metrics, run synthetic correlation tests nightly, and gather customer telemetry.

Phase 3 (opt-in strict): Offer strict mode to Dedicated customers and a preview group of Hosted tenants with dedicated alerting. Coordinate with capacity planning to adjust autoscaler thresholds.

Fallback: Toggle off at the control plane per-region; on rollback, metadata headers will still be ignored by downstream but no data loss is expected because we emit best-effort flags.
test_plan:
Unit tests for buffer eviction, watermark advancement heuristics, and overflow policies. Integration tests:
- Synthetic producer that emits correlated events with intentional reordering to validate in-order reconstruction across ingestion layers.
- End-to-end integration with Loki writer to assert tags and ordering flags are preserved.
- Fault injection: drop heartbeat markers to validate watermark stall detection and trigger backpressure path.

Load test: replay a 10k RPS multi-tenant trace with 20% hot correlation ids and measure ordering percentiles and latency impact. Regression tests added to CI for watermarking heuristics.
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Maya Chen. Initial spike completed; prototype for per-correlation buffer implemented in sandbox. Observed ~1.6ms median overhead for envelope encoding.
2025-02-20: Design review with runtime team. Agreed to limit correlation vector to 2 hops to reduce header size. Action: add config knob for strict vs best-effort policy (Priya).
2025-02-25: Integration spike with Loki writer showed minor schema mismatch; PR open to add 'ordering_suspect' label persistence (see PR #4782).

2025-03-01: Load test results uploaded to Confluence; under 2x burst we hit buffer overflow at 8MB default. Decided to reduce default per-correlation cap to 2MB and surface more aggressive backpressure hints.
2025-03-02: Began implementing backpressure header (X-Log-Watermark). End-to-end 429 path tests drafted. Assigned to Priya for implementation and to Ben Wallace for alerting dashboards.
Operational runbook: on prolonged watermark stalls (>30s) route tenant to degraded ingestion path and notify SRE channel #ingest-paging.
